title: Teola: Towards End-to-End Optimization of LLM-based Applications
technique: Primitive-level dataflow graph (p-graph) orchestration for LLM apps: parallelization, pipelining, topology-aware batching and app-aware scheduling across LLM and non-LLM engines

optimized_metrics.evidence: Large language model (LLM)-based applications consist of both LLM and non-LLM components, each contributing to the end-to-end latency. Despite great efforts to optimize LLM inference, end-to-end workflow optimization has been overlooked.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: average latency under varying request loads

optimized_metrics.evidence: identifying an execution plan with the best end-to-end latency
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: average latency under varying request loads

headline_claim.text: Comprehensive experiments show that Teola can achieve up to 2.09x speedup over existing systems across various popular LLM applications.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 8 (average latency vs request rate), Figs 9-10, co-location

metric_definitions.definition_quote: optimize for the total completion time instead of per-batch latency
metric_definitions.notes: Teola never formally defines 'latency'; evaluation plots 'avg latency (s)' of a whole query workflow (all modules: embedding, search, LLM prefill/decode, API calls) vs request rate. Includes queueing at engines under load ('queuing latency dominates end-to-end time').

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we can only optimize for the per-request latency with reasonable but sub-optimal GPU utilization.
metric_definitions.notes: Request-level engines optimise per-batch/per-request latency; Teola argues for total completion time of correlated requests (48 embeddings: 1.8 s -> 1.35 s with larger batch).

load_regime: Poisson request-rate sweep (req/s) of synthetic queries from web_question, HotpotQA, TruthfulQA, etc.; single-query latency also reported
tradeoff_acknowledged: Per-batch/per-invocation latency can get slightly higher while total completion time falls (batch 16 vs 4 example).
hardware: NVIDIA 3090 24GB GPUs (embeddings, 2B-13B LLMs); 2x A800 80GB for llama-30B; 100 Gbps network
workloads: Search-engine-empowered generation, naive/advanced RAG doc QA, contextual retrieval, LLM agent (apps built from LlamaIndex/Anthropic pipelines)
extractor_notes: Metric used without formal definition ('avg latency (s)' of a query's whole workflow). Baselines PO (per-invocation oriented) vs TO (throughput oriented) engine scheduling make the request-level vs app-level contrast. No TTFT/TPOT/percentiles; non-LLM modules can be >50% of E2E.
load_class_quote: Poisson distribution-based synthesis of [§6: avg latency vs request rate (req/s); single-query latency also reported]
